summary: Zambia's NDC 3.0 combines restoration, conservation and agriculture measures. For restoration, it proposes restoring 6,000,000 ha of degraded forest by 2030—about 12.5% of the current 480,317 km² forest area—and rehabilitating 600,000 ha of degraded catchments. Conservation includes expanding water-quality monitoring from 1,000 to 1,800 sites by 2030, mapping and protecting 468 ground water aquifer resources, placing 8,369,501 ha of forest under community forest management (about 17.4% of current forest), and targeting 90% of mining operations to use water-efficient processes and dry-stack tailings by 2030; separately, 80% of catchments are to have allocation plans. Agriculture targets include 150,000 ha of solar-powered irrigation, 800,000 ha under climate-smart agriculture, 120,000 ha of insured smallholder production, and a 50% reduction in post-harvest losses. Individually, those three agricultural area targets equal about 1.2%, 6.6% and 1.0% of the current 121,445 km² agricultural area, respectively.
